question: How accurately can Tubesense locate the train between stations without GPS?
norm_question: how accurately can tubesense locate the train between stations without gps

answer.text: Against a curve-edge reference, Tubesense locates the train with a 1.8 m median error over 10 forward-test runs (versus 11.2 m for a timetable baseline), or 13.5 m when yaw is hidden around each curve edge.

verified_claims.text: Against a curve-edge reference on 10 forward-test runs, Tubesense achieves a median positioning error of 1.8 m compared with 11.2 m for a timetable baseline, while the fraction of the 90 % band that contains the reference has a mean of 0.951.

When yaw is hidden around each curve edge in a leave-one-run-out evaluation over 19 Central line runs, the median positioning error against a curve-edge reference is 13.5 m, compared with 22.8 m for the timetable baseline at the same hidden curve edges.

On the pre-registered H2b test across 6 Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green runs, the positioning verdict is GO with a 1.95 m median error against a curve-edge reference and a mean of 0.963 for the fraction of the 90 % band that contains the reference.

In the v2 post-hoc evaluation using Working Timetable metres against a curve-edge reference, the median error is 2.4 m across 8 development runs (where the fraction of the 90 % band containing the reference has a mean of 0.92) and 1.8 m across 10 forward-test runs (versus 11.85 m for the timetable baseline, with a mean coverage fraction of 0.936).
